claims.text: Arc melting followed by homogenization at 1100°C for 1 hour and controlled cooling yields a uniform Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Al high-entropy matrix.
The controlled intervention is substitution of approximately 5–10 at.% Mn into the Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Al baseline alloy.
An optimized Mn addition in the proposed range can retain a single-phase alloy structure.
Mn substitution modifies local magnetic exchange interactions.
Mn incorporation alters the local electron density of the alloy.
Mn incorporation alters local magnetic coupling.
The Mn-induced electronic and magnetic changes promote magnetostructural coupling.
The proposed magnetostructural coupling produces a sharper and enhanced magnetocaloric response at fields near or below 2 T.
The Mn-alloyed material will have a statistically significant increase in magnetic entropy change relative to the Mn-free baseline.
Mn substitution will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the Mn-free baseline.
Mn substitution will not significantly disturb intrinsic heat-transfer pathways.
The Mn-alloyed alloy will maintain rapid heat exchange relative to the baseline.
The Mn-alloyed alloy will maintain mechanical performance and stability relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis is expected to apply near room temperature at applied magnetic fields up to approximately 2 T.
Keeping Mn at or below approximately 10 at.% is expected to avoid phase instability.
The proposed comparison uses Mn-free and Mn-substituted alloys prepared under the same processing conditions.
Failure to enhance the low-field magnetocaloric response, degradation of heat exchange or mechanical properties, or detection of secondary phases would falsify the hypothesis.
